title: Binary Search
description:
# Binary Search

Given an integer array `nums` sorted in strictly increasing order and an integer `target`, return the index of `target` in `nums`. If `target` is not present, return `-1`.

The required runtime complexity is `O(log n)`. You may assume every value in `nums` is unique, so there is at most one correct index.

## Example 1

**Input:** nums = [-1,0,3,5,9,12], target = 9

**Output:** 4

**Explanation:** `nums[4]` is `9`.

## Example 2

**Input:** nums = [-1,0,3,5,9,12], target = 2

**Output:** -1

**Explanation:** `2` is between existing values but does not appear in the array.

## Constraints

* `1 <= nums.length <= 10000`
* `-10000 < nums[i], target < 10000`
* All integers in `nums` are unique.
* `nums` is sorted in strictly increasing order.

tests.description: Target exists in the right half
Target near the middle of an even-length array
Two elements with target at left
Two elements with target at right
Two elements with missing target between them
Target found after repeatedly discarding the left half

solutions.name: Closed-Interval Binary Search
solutions.description:
## Approach

Maintain a closed search interval `[left, right]`, where both endpoints are still possible target positions. On every step, compare `nums[mid]` with `target` and discard the half that cannot contain the target.

## Key Insight

Because both endpoints are included, the loop condition is `left <= right`. After checking `mid`, the next interval must exclude `mid`, so the updates are `left = mid + 1` and `right = mid - 1`.

## Complexity Analysis
- Time Complexity: O(log n)
- Space Complexity: O(1)

solutions.name: Half-Open Binary Search
solutions.description:
## Approach

Maintain a half-open interval `[left, right)`, where `right` is one position past the last candidate. The search continues while at least one candidate remains, so the loop condition is `left < right`.

## Key Insight

The right endpoint is excluded. When `nums[mid]` is too large, `mid` can become the new excluded right boundary with `right = mid`; when it is too small, move the included left boundary to `mid + 1`.

## Complexity Analysis
- Time Complexity: O(log n)
- Space Complexity: O(1)

solutions.name: Lower Bound Then Check
solutions.description:
## Approach

First find the first index whose value is greater than or equal to `target`. After the loop, that insertion position is the only place where `target` could be located, so verify it before returning.

## Key Insight

This transforms exact search into a reusable boundary-search pattern. The same lower-bound loop is the foundation for first-position, insertion-position, and many range-query problems.

## Complexity Analysis
- Time Complexity: O(log n)
- Space Complexity: O(1)

solutions.name: Recursive Binary Search
solutions.description:
## Approach

Represent the current closed interval as recursive parameters. Each call handles one middle comparison, then recurses into only the half that can still contain the target.

## Key Insight

The base case `left > right` means there is no candidate left. This version directly shows the divide-and-conquer definition, while also making the recursion stack cost explicit.

## Complexity Analysis
- Time Complexity: O(log n)
- Space Complexity: O(log n)
